summary: Specializing in Iranian, Central Asian studies, and linguistics, John Gombojab Hangin studied at Hokkaido University, Columbia University, and Indiana University Bloomington. He held posts at Johns Hopkins, Georgetown, UC Berkeley, Columbia, and served as full professor at Indiana University (1965–1989).

Working in history, archaeology, and Indology, John Griffiths studied at the Royal College of Art (circa 1854–1859). He held a post at the Sir Jamsetjee Jeejebhoy School of Art from circa 1865 to 1895.
John H. Berthrong, working in Sinology, philosophy, and religious studies, completed graduate study under Alfonso Verdu. He held a post at Boston University (attested 1996).

Specializing in history, archaeology, and Indology, John Henry Hutton studied at Chigwell School and Worcester College, Oxford (circa 1904–1908). He served in the Indian Civil Service from circa 1909 to 1935.

Wright worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics, studying at Dartmouth College and the University of Leipzig under Georg Curtius. He held posts at Ohio State, Dartmouth, Johns Hopkins, Harvard (circa 1887–1908), and the American School of Classical Studies at Athens.

John Herbert Harington worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He served as secretary (1790) and president (1825–1828) of The Asiatic Society, and as an honorary professor at Fort William College from circa 1801 to 1823.
John Hope studied at the University of Edinburgh from circa 1740 to 1750 and held an academic post there from circa 1761 to 1786.

Working in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Crook studied at Southampton, Cambridge under Robert Hinde and William Homan Thorpe, and under Sheng Yen. He held posts at Bristol (circa 1963–1995), CASBS, and the Université Bouddhique Européenne.

Working in philosophy and Buddhist studies, John J. Holder studied under Harry Krebs. He held a visiting research appointment at the University of Oxford and posts at St. Norbert College (attested 2006 and 2018).

Makransky works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under numerous teachers, including Lobsang Tendzin and Geshe Lhundup Sopa. He held posts at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, Boston College, and Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

Working in Indology and Buddhist studies, John James Jones was educated at Aberystwyth University. He served as Deputy-Keeper in the Department of Printed Books at the National Library of Wales from circa 1926 to 1957.

John Jorgensen works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He has held positions as a researcher at Australian National University, taught Japanese Studies at Griffith University, and served as Senior Research Associate at La Trobe University (attested 2019).

Specializing in Buddhist studies and Sinology, John Kieschnick held an academic post at the University of Bristol from circa 2005 to 2011 before joining the faculty at Stanford University in circa 2011.

John Lane Bell is a philosopher who studied at the University of Oxford (circa 1963–1968). He held posts at the London School of Economics (circa 1968–1989), the National University of Singapore (circa 1987–1988), and the University of Western Ontario (circa 1989).

John Leyden worked in linguistics and Indology, studying under Henry Thomas Colebrooke from circa 1805 to 1810. He served as assistant secretary and secretary of The Asiatic Society between circa 1809 and 1811.

Kipling worked in history, archaeology, and Indology, having studied at Woodhouse Grove School. He taught at Sir Jamsetjee Jeejebhoy School of Art (circa 1865–1875) and served as Principal of the National College of Arts and Curator of Lahore Museum (1875–1893).

John M. Koller worked in philosophy, Indology, and religious studies, studying at the East-West Center under Shri Krishna Saksena, Charles Alexander Moore, and George T. Artola. He served as a professor of philosophy at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute.

Rosenfield, who worked in history, archaeology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies, earned degrees from several universities, completing his PhD at Harvard under Benjamin Rowland. He held posts at Iowa, UCLA, Harvard University (1965–1991), Harvard Art Museums, and the Fogg Museum.

Working in history, archaeology, and Indology, Marshall studied at Cambridge, the British School at Athens, and under Arthur Evans. He served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1902–1931) and was an honorary fellow at King's College, Cambridge.

John Muir studied at East India Company College, Glasgow, and Bonn. He served in the Bengal Civil Service (1828–1853), was principal at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University in 1844, and later held a post at the University of Edinburgh.
